missing_clause_policy.rationale: A missing governing-law provision leaves dispute-planning uncertainty under the documented procurement rubric.

categories.abstain_rationale: The clause does not identify a stable governing jurisdiction or contains terms outside the documented jurisdiction list.

present_rules.rationale: The project playbook escalates a unilateral counterparty right to change the governing law.

when_any: \bgoverned by the laws? of (?:the )?(?:United Kingdom|European Union)\b
present_rules.rationale: A non-U.S. governing law is a medium review escalation under this U.S. procurement baseline, not an enforceability judgment.

when_any: \blaws? of (?:the )?(?:(?:State|Commonwealth) of )?(?:Alabama|Alaska|Arizona|Arkansas|California|Colorado|Connecticut|Delaware|Florida|Georgia|Hawaii|Idaho|Illinois|Indiana|Iowa|Kansas|Kentucky|Louisiana|Maine|Maryland|Massachusetts|Michigan|Minnesota|Mississippi|Missouri|Montana|Nebraska|Nevada|New Hampshire|New Jersey|New Mexico|New York|North Carolina|North Dakota|Ohio|Oklahoma|Oregon|Pennsylvania|Rhode Island|South Carolina|South Dakota|Tennessee|Texas|Utah|Vermont|Virginia|Washington|West Virginia|Wisconsin|Wyoming)\b
present_rules.rationale: The clause identifies U.S. state or D.C. law and does not trigger the documented jurisdiction escalation.
Federal-law-only wording receives a low escalation because the applicable state law remains unclear.
A governing jurisdiction is present but falls outside the documented U.S.-state resolver, so it receives medium manual review rather than an inferred legal conclusion.

missing_rules.rationale: the documented procurement rubric treats an omitted governing-law provision as a medium review escalation.

missing_clause_policy.rationale: Renewal absence is optional and unscored; it must not be encoded as numeric zero.

categories.abstain_rationale: The renewal text does not state enough about duration, control, or exit timing for the documented rules.

present_rules.rationale: Supplier-only, indefinite, or multi-year automatic renewal is a hard-stop escalation under the buyer-side rubric.
Automatic renewal with no visible exit mechanism receives a medium escalation.
A renewal period of at most one year with an express exit receives a low playbook escalation.

when_any: \bparties may mutually agree in writing to renew\b
present_rules.rationale: Renewal controlled by mutual written agreement does not trigger a buyer-side escalation.
The text shows a bounded renewal structure, but party control is unresolved; it receives a low review label with low confidence.
A renewal mechanism is present but duration, control, or exit cannot be fully resolved from the annotated provision; medium denotes required human review.

missing_rules.rationale: No renewal provision was identified; optional absence is excluded from the numeric severity target.

missing_clause_policy.rationale: Revenue-sharing absence is not a deviation unless another economic obligation makes it expected.

categories.abstain_rationale: The text does not resolve payer, recipient, calculation base, or verification rights.

present_rules.rationale: A buyer payment calculated unilaterally by the counterparty is a hard-stop economic-control issue.
A buyer-side revenue share with no visible verification mechanism receives a medium escalation.
A defined net-revenue base paired with verification language is a low residual review item.
The identified payment runs to the reviewed buyer, so this rule alone assigns no buyer-side risk.
A variable-payment formula is visible but the reviewed-party direction is unresolved; the rule assigns low review priority with low confidence.
Variable economics are present but payer, base, duration, or verification remains unresolved; medium means human review is required.

missing_rules.rationale: No revenue-sharing obligation was identified, so this category is not applicable absent an external economic trigger.

missing_clause_policy.rationale: the buyer-side rubric expects a liability cap in ongoing commercial contracts but does not infer applicability for unknown types.

categories.abstain_rationale: The cap language does not identify enough scope, amount basis, or party allocation to apply the buyer playbook.

present_rules.rationale: Project policy treats an unlimited buyer exposure paired with a counterparty cap as a hard-stop escalation.
A supplier cap at one quarter of the stated fee base is below the documented buyer-policy floor.
A lesser-of cap or exclusive-remedy formulation receives a medium buyer-side escalation.
A clearly mutual monetary cap is a minor buyer-playbook deviation pending review of amount and carve-outs.
A facially mutual exclusion of specified damages receives low review priority pending its interaction with carve-outs.
A monetary limitation is visible but party allocation or adequacy is unresolved; medium denotes required human review.

when_all: \b(?:in no event|shall not be liable|limitation of liability|not liable for)\b
present_rules.rationale: A damages limitation is present but direction, cap basis, or carve-outs are unresolved; medium is a review-priority label, not a legal judgment.

missing_rules.rationale: the buyer-side rubric escalates a missing liability cap in an ongoing commercial contract.
the cap-absence rule is not applied to this contract type.

missing_clause_policy.rationale: Uncapped-liability absence is optional and unscored; it must not be encoded as numeric zero.

categories.abstain_rationale: The text does not resolve whose liability is uncapped or the scope of the carve-out.

present_rules.rationale: General uncapped buyer liability is a hard-stop under the buyer-side rubric.
A material buyer-side carve-out from the cap is High review priority under the buyer-side rubric.
An uncapped carve-out limited to buyer payment or tax obligations is a low residual review item.
Only the supplier's exposure is identified as uncapped, so this rule does not escalate buyer risk.
The visible mutual carve-out is limited to standard serious-misconduct or personal-injury claims, so this rule alone does not escalate.

when_all: \b(?:except|excluded from|shall not apply|does not apply|not limit|nothing.{0,60}(?:exclude|limit))\b
present_rules.rationale: A material cap carve-out is visible but party allocation is unresolved; Medium requires human review without inventing a buyer-side High exposure.
An exception to a liability limitation is present but its scope or party direction is unresolved; medium is a triage label.

missing_rules.rationale: No uncapped-liability provision was identified; optional absence is excluded from the numeric severity target.

missing_clause_policy.rationale: the buyer-side rubric expects a buyer exit right in ongoing commercial contracts.

categories.abstain_rationale: The clause does not resolve which party may terminate, notice timing, or exit charges.

when_all: \b(?:supplier|vendor|licensor|provider) may terminate.{0,80}(?:for convenience|without cause|for any reason)\b
\b(?:customer|buyer|licensee|client) may not terminate.{0,80}(?:for convenience|without cause|for any reason)\b
present_rules.rationale: A supplier-only convenience exit is a hard-stop buyer asymmetry.

when_all: \b(?:remaining fees|all fees due|early termination fee|termination charge)\b
present_rules.rationale: An exit conditioned on remaining-term fees does not provide an effective buyer convenience termination.
A buyer convenience right requiring more than ninety days' notice is a medium deviation.
A buyer-controlled exit on no more than thirty days' notice and no visible penalty meets the documented target.
A buyer or mutual exit on forty-five to ninety days' notice is a low deviation.
A mutual termination right with notice and no visible exit charge receives low review priority.
The clause provides a penalty-free exit but the reviewed-party holder is unresolved; it receives a low-confidence Low label.

when_any: \bterminate(?:d|s|ion)?\b.{0,160}\b(?:at any time|without cause|for convenience|sole discretion|written notice)\b
present_rules.rationale: A convenience-style exit is present but the reviewed-party holder or cost is unresolved; medium means human review is required.

missing_rules.rationale: An ongoing commercial contract without a buyer convenience exit receives a medium escalation.
the missing-convenience-termination policy is not applied to this contract type.

missing_clause_policy.rationale: Anti-assignment absence is optional and unscored; it must not be encoded as numeric zero.

categories.abstain_rationale: The text does not resolve consent symmetry or affiliate, successor, and change-of-control exceptions.

present_rules.rationale: An absolute buyer restriction paired with a supplier assignment right is a hard-stop asymmetry.
Buyer consent restrictions without ordinary corporate carve-outs receive a medium escalation.
A mutual restriction with ordinary corporate carve-outs is a low residual review item.
The buyer retains ordinary corporate assignment flexibility while the supplier remains restricted.
A facially mutual consent restriction receives low review priority pending confirmation of corporate carve-outs.
The consent standard is bounded but the restricted party is unresolved; this receives a low-confidence Low label.
An assignment-consent restriction is present but party asymmetry and carve-outs are unresolved; medium means human review is required.

missing_rules.rationale: No anti-assignment provision was identified; optional absence is excluded from the numeric severity target.

missing_clause_policy.rationale: Audit-right absence becomes material when a linked payment or compliance duty requires verification.

categories.abstain_rationale: The clause does not resolve the auditing party, frequency, scope, notice, or cost allocation.

present_rules.rationale: Multiple intrusive dimensions in a supplier audit right create a high operational escalation.
A supplier audit of the buyer without visible safeguards receives a medium escalation.
A bounded buyer audit right supports verification without triggering a buyer-side escalation.
A mutual, bounded audit right is a low residual review item.
The audit right contains a visible procedural safeguard, but the reviewed-party direction is unresolved; it receives low review priority.
An audit or inspection right is present but holder, scope, frequency, or cost remains unresolved; medium denotes required human review.

missing_rules.rationale: A linked variable-payment provision lacks a CUAD-annotated audit or verification right, so the buyer-side playbook requires medium human review.
Audit-right absence is not scored without a linked verification need; cross-category logic may override this result.

missing_clause_policy.rationale: the buyer-side rubric expects use rights in license-dependent agreements but not in every service contract.

categories.abstain_rationale: The text does not resolve grant direction, licensed subject matter, or material scope limitations.

present_rules.rationale: A buyer-to-supplier grant with at least three broad scope attributes is a hard-stop IP escalation.
A buyer-to-supplier grant with multiple breadth attributes receives a medium escalation.
A buyer content license limited to performing the services is a low residual review item.
The supplier grants the buyer an express non-exclusive use right, so this rule does not escalate risk.
The grant contains at least three breadth attributes, but grant direction is unresolved; medium denotes required IP review.
A bounded grant is visible but party direction is unresolved; it receives low review priority.
A license grant is present but grant direction or material scope is unresolved; medium is a triage label requiring human review.

missing_rules.rationale: A license-dependent agreement without an identified license grant receives a medium escalation.
the missing-license rule is not applied to this non-license contract type.

missing_clause_policy.rationale: Exclusivity absence is optional and unscored; it must not be encoded as numeric zero.

categories.abstain_rationale: The text does not resolve the bound party, duration, scope, or exit conditions.

present_rules.rationale: The buyer-side party receives the exclusive right, so the clause is not treated as an adverse buyer commitment.
A facially mutual exclusive grant receives low review priority rather than an adverse buyer label.

when_all: \b(?:purchase exclusively|exclusively purchase|all requirements|sole supplier|shall not.{0,80}(?:other source|other supplier|competitor))\b
present_rules.rationale: A long, indefinite, all-requirements, or sole-source buyer commitment is a hard-stop escalation.
A one-year-or-shorter buyer commitment conditioned on performance is a low residual review item.

when_all: \b(?:purchase exclusively|exclusively purchase|exclusive source|exclusive supplier|shall not.{0,80}(?:other source|other supplier|competitor))\b
present_rules.rationale: Buyer exclusivity without a clearly bounded, performance-conditioned scope receives a medium escalation.
Only the supplier is identified as bound for the buyer's benefit, so this rule does not escalate buyer risk.
A restriction on alternative sources or competing activity is visible, but party role or scope is incomplete; medium requires human review.
An exclusive appointment or grant is visible but the reviewed-party benefit or burden is unresolved; it receives low review priority.
An exclusivity commitment is present but the bound party, scope, duration, or exit is unresolved; medium is a triage label, not a competition-law conclusion.

missing_rules.rationale: No exclusivity provision was identified; optional absence is excluded from the numeric severity target.
